authoredFrom: PS-B25 — a quoted module path is a PATH EXPRESSION, not the first variable inside it. Authored 2026-10-27 from the whole-population reconciliation (validation/m14/fixtures/powershell/reconcile-f5.mts), where the class measured 209 `imports` + 203 `references` rows: `Import-Module "$PSScriptRoot/../../tools/ci.psm1"` published the variable `PSScriptRoot` as the module, while the unquoted spelling of the same path was published whole. The grammar wraps every quoted argument as `array_literal_expression > unary_expression > string_literal`, so the argument reader's first-variable search answered before the string was read as a string. The fix keeps the variable handoff ONLY when the whole quoted value is that variable (`"$t"`, the PS29 case, where the value must stay the bare name because a `$`-prefixed uses target is the F9 defect) and otherwise publishes the path text with its sigils. The four forbid rows are the pre-fix shape (`here`, `PSScriptRoot`) and the dynamic-name family (`dynamic`): `Import-Module $m` names no module the graph can join.

expectSymbols.comment: a function parameter is declared as a VARIABLE in this lane (the analyzer has no Parameter kind for it); the containment is what makes the owner explicit

expectRelationships.comment: the QUOTED path expression: the module is the whole path, sigil included. Pre-fix this row was `imports -> here`.
quoted, with an AUTOMATIC variable: the path is still the path. Pre-fix this row was `imports -> PSScriptRoot`.
the UNQUOTED control: a `generic_token` was always published whole, so this row is what the two quoted forms had to be made to agree with.
PS23 keeps BOTH labels for one load: `imports` is the dependency and `references` the name resolution. Both carry the same target, so the two rows cannot describe different facts.

`Import-Module $dynamic` names no module; what the file does is READ the variable. That read is the honest edge, and it is why the forbid rows below refuse an import to it. The import branch `break`s before the command branch's generic argument read, so this row was published by nothing at all before the fix — the same defect class the F9 argument-read note records, on the one branch that skipped that pass.

the PATH EXPRESSION also READS the variable inside it: the module is the path, and `$here` is read to build it. Both facts are true and they are different edges — this is why the fix could not be "publish the text instead of the variable": it has to publish the text AND keep the read.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: exactly the three path expressions. A reader that published the first variable instead would also read 3 — which is why the forbid rows exist; a reader that also published the dynamic name would read 4.
